mc.prompt: Why must a negative genetic test be interpreted within its scope?
mc.answer: Untested variants or causes may still exist
mc.explanation: The test answers specific questions, not every possible genetic question.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Negative always means no DNA is present
Tests cannot ever provide useful evidence
Untested variants or causes may still exist
All conditions have one identical allele

mc.explanation: Understanding uses, risks and options matters before agreement.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Whether every participant will have the same phenotype
Whether the test can replace all medical history
Only whether the collection tube is coloured
How samples and results may be used and shared

writing.prompt: Distinguish a positive risk-associated test result from a guaranteed phenotype.
writing.model: A result may identify a variant associated with increased probability, but expression can depend on penetrance, other genetic factors and environment. The test’s validation and scope determine how strongly it predicts an outcome. Increased risk is not automatically certainty.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.
Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: Identify two issues a participant should understand before consenting to a genetic study and explain why.
writing.model: The participant should understand what is tested and what results may mean, including uncertainty. They should also understand how samples and data may be stored, used or shared, because genetic information can have personal and family implications. Consent supports an informed choice.

worked.title: Interpret a limited negative result
worked.scenario: A fictional test detects none of three specified variants associated with one condition.
steps: The result establishes that those tested variants were not detected under the test’s conditions.
It does not rule out every untested variant, every different genetic condition or every environmental cause.
Interpretation requires the test’s scope and limitations.
A personal decision should be informed by appropriate counselling rather than a blanket classroom rule.
